context: A uni student interviews a retired civil engineer
purpose: Teach: 交通省/官邸/直線/遠隔/無関心/団地/下降/上流

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 長年、土木と交通省の橋渡しをされていたんですよね。
lines.en: You've spent years bridging civil engineering and the transport ministry, haven't you?
lines.style: Respectful, genuinely curious. Leaning forward slightly. Careful articulation — this is someone asking an elder about his life's work. Warm but formal.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。官邸とも何度も交渉した。
lines.en: Yes. I negotiated with the cabinet office many times.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact recollection. Steady, unhurried pace. No pride, no regret — just stating what happened. The voice of someone who knows what he's seen.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 直線道路と団地開発の調整、住民の無関心、課題でしたか。
lines.en: Was coordinating road projects and housing developments difficult because residents just didn't engage?
lines.style: Thoughtful probe, not accusatory. Slow on the setup. Slight lift on the final clause — testing whether he agrees with the diagnosis.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。遠隔地ほど、住民の声が下降していった。
lines.en: Yes. The more remote the area, the quieter the voices became.
lines.style: Quiet, observational tone. Voice trails slightly at the end. Speaking from memory — not bitterness, but recognition of a pattern he watched happen.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 上流の自治体の対応、変わってきましたか。
lines.en: Have upstream municipalities started responding differently now?
lines.style: Genuine interest, not leading. Open-ended. Lean into the question naturally — Ren is following the thread of what matters to this man.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 近年は、改善しているよ。
lines.en: Things have been improving in recent years.
lines.style: Quiet affirmation with a hint of cautious optimism. Measured pace. A gentle close — not triumphant, but satisfied that direction matters more than arrival.
